# Target Loading — EARS Specs

*Brownfield specs generated by `/map-codebase` on 2026-10-15 from HEAD
`a6395d7`. They describe what the code does today.*

## How to read these specs

**Status markers**
- `[x]`: the behavior is **observed in source** at the cited location. That
  is all it means. It does not mean the behavior is tested, that a test
  passes, or that the design choice behind it is approved.

  Brownfield `[x]` entries describe current implementation behavior, not
  approved future requirements. A spec tagged `intent: none`,
  `intent: inferred`, `code-documented`, or approved only as a recorded
  current seam is a description of today's code. It is not a permanent design
  constraint just because it appears here. Changing such behavior is a normal
  design decision, made in the LLD, which then updates or deletes the spec.
- `[ ]`: an **approved intent** (stated in CLAUDE.md or docs/) that the code
  does not meet today. The spec states the required outcome only. Where the
  mechanism is undecided, the spec points to the open question that owns
  that decision.
- `[D]`: a deliberate exclusion backed by an explicit design decision.
  There are none in this segment.

**Basis tags** (in brackets after each spec)
- `obs:` the source location where the behavior was observed.
- `test:` a test that asserts the behavior, or `none`.
  - Tests marked *case* live under `cases/performing-rigs/test/`. They need
    case firmware or artifacts, and skip when those are absent.
  - No tests were executed during mapping. A cited test means an assertion
    exists, not that it passes.
- `intent:` where the intent comes from:
  - `approved (doc §)`: stated in CLAUDE.md or docs/;
  - `code-documented`: stated only in a code comment or docstring, not
    confirmed by the authors;
  - `inferred`: read from the code by the mapper;
  - `none`: observed behavior with no stated intent.

Unverified intents are not written as specs. One example is Open
Question 11: whether every Macaw discovery caller applies the Thumb policy.
The THUMB specs below are therefore scoped to the specific helper and
architecture configuration that implement the policy. The open question
stays in the LLD.

## Memory image (Macaw)

- [x] **PROD-TGT-MEM-001**: The memory builder shall map the raw firmware image, unmodified, as one read/execute segment whose first byte is at the caller-supplied flash base. [obs: `src/APTrace/FirmwareLoader.hs:60-70` · test: case `cases/performing-rigs/test/Main.hs` tests 3–5 (exercised, not asserted) · intent: code-documented (`FirmwareLoader.hs:52-55`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-MEM-002**: The memory builder shall map a zero-initialized read/write RAM segment at the caller-supplied RAM base and size. [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:71-77` · test: none · intent: code-documented as a deliberate simplification (`FirmwareLoader.hs:57-59`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-MEM-003**: If two memory segments overlap, then the memory builder shall return an error and no memory image. [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:76-80, 103-105` · test: none · intent: none]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-MEM-004**: Where an MMIO range is supplied to the MMIO-aware builder, the memory builder shall add a zero-initialized read/write segment covering that range. [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:89-105` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`FirmwareLoader.hs:82-88`)]

## Thumb execution-state policy

- [x] **PROD-TGT-THUMB-001**: When an address is passed to the `macawCortexMEntry` helper, or to `resolveEntries` (which applies it to each vector-table root), the helper shall return the address with its low (Thumb) bit set, leaving an already-set bit unchanged. Whether every Macaw discovery caller applies this helper is not established (LLD Open Question 11). [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:137-138, 193` · test: case `Main.hs` tests 1, 2, 5 · intent: approved (`docs/tooling/tool-selection.md` "Operating rules": Cortex-M is Thumb-only)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-THUMB-002**: When an address is resolved to a Macaw segment offset, the system shall not modify its low bit. [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:107-115` · test: case `Main.hs` test 3 · intent: code-documented (`FirmwareLoader.hs:109-113`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-THUMB-003**: While Macaw discovery runs with the `armCortexMInfo` architecture configuration, that configuration shall initialize each discovered function's PSTATE_T to Thumb. Whether every Macaw discovery caller uses `armCortexMInfo` is not established (LLD Open Question 11). [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:174-176` · test: case `Main.hs` test 9 (needs case firmware) · intent: approved (`tool-selection.md` "Operating rules") and code-documented (`FirmwareLoader.hs:146-155`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-THUMB-004**: If Macaw cannot resolve a block's PSTATE_T precondition while discovery runs with the `armCortexMInfo` architecture configuration, then that configuration shall treat the block as Thumb. Coverage of other discovery callers is not established (LLD Open Question 11). [obs: `FirmwareLoader.hs:177-180` · test: case `Main.hs` test 10 (needs case firmware) · intent: code-documented (`FirmwareLoader.hs:156-161`)]

## Vector table and code roots

- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-001**: The Haskell vector-table parser shall read `16 + numIrq` little-endian 32-bit words starting at image offset 0, where `numIrq` is supplied by the caller. [obs: `src/APTrace/VectorTable.hs:47-58` · test: case `Main.hs` test 5 (exercised) · intent: code-documented (`VectorTable.hs:1-3`, `:47`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-002**: The Haskell vector-table parser shall omit index 0 (the initial stack pointer) and every zero-valued word, and shall return each other entry's raw value with its Thumb bit preserved. [obs: `VectorTable.hs:50-55, 21-24` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`VectorTable.hs:41-46`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-003**: The Haskell vector-table parser shall name indices 1–15 with ARMv7-M system-handler names and higher indices `IRQ<n>_Handler`, where n = index − 16. [obs: `VectorTable.hs:27-39` · test: none · intent: none]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-004**: If the image is shorter than `16 + numIrq` words, then the Haskell vector-table parser shall fail instead of returning a partial table. [obs: `VectorTable.hs:58` (`runGet` over a fixed word count) · test: none · intent: none]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-005**: If the Ghidra vector-table seeding pre-script is run without a vector-word count, then it shall fail. [obs: `tools/ghidra/scripts/APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:50-53` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:19-23`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-006**: When the Ghidra vector-table seeding pre-script runs, it shall disassemble and create a function at the bit-0-cleared target of each vector word after the initial stack pointer that is neither `0` nor `0xFFFFFFFF` and whose target lies within the program's first memory block. [obs: `APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:56-76` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:1-16`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-007**: Where extra seed addresses are passed to the Ghidra vector-table seeding pre-script, it shall seed each one at the address exactly as given, without clearing its low bit. [obs: `APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:78-87` · test: none · intent: none (see LLD Open Question 9)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-008**: If seeding one address fails in the Ghidra vector-table seeding pre-script, then the pre-script shall print the failure and continue with the remaining addresses. [obs: `APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:37-45` · test: none · intent: none (see LLD Open Question 1)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-009**: When run without `--scan`, the vector-table scanner prototype shall score only image offset 0. With `--scan`, it shall score every 4-byte-aligned offset below the scan limit. [obs: `tools/vector_scan.py:151-160` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`vector_scan.py:12-14`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-VEC-010**: If no candidate scores at least 4, then the vector-table scanner prototype shall report that none was found and exit with status 1. Otherwise it shall dump the highest-scoring table. [obs: `vector_scan.py:159-174` · test: none · intent: none]

## Persistent Ghidra project and cache identity

- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-001**: The Ghidra backend shall keep one persistent analyzed Ghidra project per registered firmware key, in a per-key directory under its cache root. [obs: `tools/ghidra/aptrace_ghidra.py:123-124, 218-227, 230-287` · test: `tools/ghidra/test_aptrace_ghidra.py:37-41` · intent: approved (`docs/tooling/ghidra-backend.md`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-002**: When the Ghidra backend builds a project, it shall do the following in order:
  1. import the registered image with Ghidra's BinaryLoader at the registered load base, language `ARM:LE:32:Cortex` and compiler spec `default`;
  2. run the vector-table seeding pre-script with the configured vector-word count and any derived seeds;
  3. run auto-analysis with a 300-second per-file timeout;
  4. apply provenance labels when the image's provenance TSV exists;
  5. write the static-analysis export, then the census export.

  [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:253-279` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:37-41` (build succeeds, exercised) · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:230-235`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-003**: The Ghidra backend's cache identity shall consist of:
  - firmware key, repository-relative path and SHA-256;
  - load base, processor and compiler spec;
  - Ghidra version and the manual analysis version;
  - the vector-word count passed to seeding;
  - the content hash of each Ghidra build script;
  - the provenance-TSV hash, or null when none is configured;
  - the derived-seeds hash, only when a derived-seeds file exists.

  [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:159-160, 171-195` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:72-117` (script and TSV changes alter identity) · intent: approved (`ghidra-backend.md`) and code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:18-30`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-004**: If a build script or configured provenance TSV does not exist, then the Ghidra backend shall record the sentinel `"missing"` as its hash in the cache identity. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:163-168, 187-190` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:164-167`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-005**: The Ghidra backend shall classify a cache as `missing` when it has no recorded identity, `stale` when any recorded identity field differs from the expected identity, and `fresh` otherwise. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:206-215` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:39-41, 89-94, 126-127` · intent: approved (`ghidra-backend.md`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-006**: If the cache for a firmware key is `missing` or `stale`, then the Ghidra backend shall refuse every query that reads the project or its exports, with an instruction to build or rebuild, instead of answering from the cache. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:290-297, 303, 332, 341` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:128-133` · intent: approved (`ghidra-backend.md`) and code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:28-30`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-007**: While the cache for a firmware key is `fresh`, the Ghidra backend shall not rebuild it unless a rebuild is explicitly requested. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:236-240, 528-531` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:38` (exercised) · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:233-235`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-008**: When the Ghidra backend rebuilds a `stale` cache, it shall report each identity field whose cached and expected values differ, then delete the cache directory before building. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:241-251` · test: none · intent: none]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-009**: When a Ghidra build completes, the Ghidra backend shall write the cache identity, computed at that time, as the project's `meta.json`. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:281-283` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:41` · intent: none (see LLD Open Question 3)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-010**: If a firmware key's derived-seeds file records a firmware SHA-256 other than the registered image's, then the Ghidra backend shall refuse to build. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:138-149` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:139-140`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-011**: When a provenance TSV is applied during a Ghidra build, the system shall rename, as user-defined, each function that exists at a row's single `0x`-prefixed address, and comment it with the row's classification. Rows without such an address, or with no function at it, shall be skipped and counted. [obs: `tools/ghidra/scripts/APTraceApplyProvenance.java:44-85` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`APTraceApplyProvenance.java:1-22`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-012**: When a decompile or disassembly query is answered, the Ghidra backend shall reopen the persistent project in no-analysis, read-only mode, without re-importing or re-analyzing. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:300-328` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:43-52` (timing bound only) · intent: approved (`ghidra-backend.md`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-013**: When a callers, cross-reference, containing-function or symbol query is answered, the Ghidra backend shall answer from the cached static export without invoking Ghidra. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:350-425` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:54-66` · intent: approved (`ghidra-backend.md`) and code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:13-16`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-014**: When a containing-function query names an address beyond the preceding function's recorded size, the Ghidra backend shall report the function and flag that the address lies past its recorded size. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:386-408` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:64-66` (in-range case only) · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:387-390`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-015**: When a raw literal or dump query is answered, the Ghidra backend shall read the registered image bytes at the address minus the registered load base, and shall refuse a range outside the image. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:428-463` · test: `test_aptrace_ghidra.py:68-70` (in-range case only) · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:429-431`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-016**: The Ghidra headless locator shall search for `analyzeHeadless` on PATH, then under `$GHIDRA_HOME/support`, then in Homebrew's Ghidra install, and shall report none when all three fail. [obs: `tools/ghidra/headless.py:17-31` · test: none · intent: code-documented (`headless.py:18`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-GH-017**: If no version can be parsed from the resolved `analyzeHeadless` path, then the Ghidra backend shall record the Ghidra version as `"unknown"`. [obs: `headless.py:34-44` · test: none · intent: code-documented as best-effort (`headless.py:35-40`); adequacy open (LLD Open Question 2)]
- [ ] **PROD-TGT-GH-018**: If, during a Ghidra build, any of the following happens, then the system shall make that outcome distinguishable, to consumers of the cached project and its exports, from a build in which every step completed:
  - a requested seed address cannot be seeded;
  - a provenance row cannot be applied;
  - auto-analysis does not complete within its timeout.

  [obs: unmet: seeding and labeling failures are printed only (`APTraceSeedVectorTable.java:42-44`, `APTraceApplyProvenance.java:72-76`); timeout not surfaced (`aptrace_ghidra.py:265`); none reaches `meta.json` (`:281-283`) · test: none · intent: approved (CLAUDE.md "Evidence discipline": incompleteness must be represented, never treated as no result). The representation, its location and the treatment of existing caches are undecided (LLD Open Question 1).]

## Target configuration and wiring

[obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:82-86, 113-120, 276-277` · test: none · intent: approved as a recorded current seam (`docs/case-boundary.md` "Intentional current seams"); target design open (LLD Open Questions 5–6)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-CFG-002**: The Ghidra backend shall pass `15 + external IRQ count` as the vector-word count to the seeding pre-script. [obs: `aptrace_ghidra.py:91, 263` · test: case `cases/performing-rigs/test/test_target_irq_count.py` (`test_irq_count_is_target_configuration`) · intent: code-documented (`aptrace_ghidra.py:88-90`)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-CFG-003**: The Haskell CLI shall supply the Performing Rigs case's flash base, RAM base and size, external IRQ count and MMIO window to every subcommand that needs them. A command-line flash-base override shall be accepted only for `run`, `explore`, `solve`, `macaw-census` and `macaw-census-expand`. [obs: `app/Main.hs:18, 33-59` · test: none · intent: approved as a recorded current seam (`docs/case-boundary.md`); target design open (LLD Open Question 6)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-CFG-004**: The Haskell framework library build shall compile the Performing Rigs case sources together with the framework modules. [obs: `aptrace.cabal:19-22` · test: none · intent: approved as a recorded current seam (`docs/case-boundary.md`); target design open (LLD Open Question 7)]
- [x] **PROD-TGT-CFG-005**: The external IRQ count used by the Python tools shall equal the highest interrupt number in the case SVD plus one, and shall equal the Haskell case module's `numIrq`. [obs: `cases/performing-rigs/config/performing_rigs.py` (`_svd_num_external_irq`) · test: case `test_target_irq_count.py` · intent: code-documented (`performing_rigs.py` IRQ-count comment)]
